headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and data-leakage via shared local filesystem/clipboard and broad network egress; no direct evidence of a safer isolated bridge.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor ingests workspace files, open editor buffers, clipboard, and MCP outputs; Haystack can also use MCP and REST APIs. Cursor’s shared_state_with_other_instances via local filesystem creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content from Haystack can be treated as instructions. No direct sandbox evidence exists, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF Haystack writes untrusted text into a shared workspace file or MCP response that Cursor reads
IF Cursor parses copied content or file content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable shared workspace access between the two agents
Require manual review before Cursor acts on any Haystack-produced text
Use separate MCP servers or credentials per agent
Turn off clipboard-based transfer between agents
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all inter-agent content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, clipboard contents, and has broad network egress to model providers and MCP servers; Haystack also has broad network egress and MCP access. If both operate on the same workspace, sensitive code or clipboard data can flow from Cursor into Haystack outputs or external APIs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default use, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same local workspace
IF Cursor or Haystack forwards file contents to external model providers or REST/MCP endpoints
mitigations: Separate workspaces and OS users for each agent
Avoid opening secrets or regulated data in Cursor while Haystack is connected
Restrict outbound network destinations for both agents
Clear clipboard before switching agents
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss prevention rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor can write the filesystem, modify git state, execute shell commands, and bypass approval in Yolo mode; Haystack can use MCP and broad network egress. On a shared local filesystem, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide, and uncertainty about Haystack’s write path escalates because the profile does not prove it is read-only. The overlap is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF Haystack is configured with any write-capable MCP tool or REST action
IF both agents modify the same repository or directory concurrently
mitigations: Run the agents in separate clones or directories
Disable Cursor Yolo mode for shared repos
Serialize git writes with a lock file
Limit Haystack to read-only retrieval tools
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor’s agent loop can generate code or actions from Haystack-provided search/RAG outputs, and Haystack can surface retrieved text through MCP or APIs. If Cursor treats those outputs as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect code or actions. Haystack is not documented here as a verifier, so the safer assumption is a medium-risk dependency chain.
conditions: IF Cursor consumes Haystack retrieval results as facts without a verification step
IF Haystack returns stale or irrelevant passages that Cursor then uses to edit code
mitigations: Require source links for every Haystack claim before Cursor acts
Add a human review step for generated edits
Constrain Haystack to retrieval-only mode
Ask Cursor to cross-check critical facts against primary sources
requires-engineering: implement citation validation

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor explicitly handles source code, open files, and clipboard contents, while Haystack only lists anonymous usage statistics. No residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented, and Haystack’s profile does not show PHI or EU-PII handling. Because the pairwise compliance pathway is not evidenced, the risk stays low rather than medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Cursor and then routed through Haystack-backed services
IF deployment policy requires residency controls that are not configured for either agent
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Review vendor privacy and retention settings
Use separate tenants or projects for sensitive work
Document data-flow boundaries
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing
